title: The significance of PET/CT combined with machine learning models for the classification of lymphoma involvement and metastases in enlarged lymph nodes.
summary: Original full text, Methods/Results: RF/SVM/ANN classified lymphoma involvement versus metastasis in 247 pathology-confirmed PET/CT nodes from 85 patients; RF AUC .942 with bootstrap/permutation assessment. Small, single-center internal evaluation. The result is reported in Frontiers in Oncology. The study does not establish generalization beyond its reported setting or prospective real-world benefit.
ai_technology: Random-forest, support-vector-machine and artificial-neural-network classifiers combined PET/CT metabolic and anatomical features to distinguish lymphoma-involved nodes from solid-tumor metastases.

evidence.tested: Original full text, Methods/Results: RF/SVM/ANN classified lymphoma involvement versus metastasis in 247 pathology-confirmed PET/CT nodes from 85 patients; RF AUC .942 with bootstrap/permutation assessment. Small, single-center internal evaluation.
evidence.unknown: Independent replication and prospective real-world benefit are not established in the reviewed study.
